sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry in both studies; CD5HA2 used successfully for FACS-based cell sorting of human T cells; CD5Flag2 showed surface expression levels comparable to or better than CD24-based controls. CD52's own biological function (complement-mediated lysis target) was NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: Python search locates SQTSSP at canonical positions 30–35 and GQNDT at 25–29, placing the tag junction unambiguously after residue 29 (T) with residue_after = S (pos 30). The NDT N-glycosylation sequon (N27-D28-T29) is preserved upstream of the insertion. The replaced stretch (SQTSSP, 30–35) contains no N-glycosylation sequon, no disulfide cysteine, and no known functional motif. CD52 has no TM helix (GPI-anchored), so there is no TM-proximity constraint to violate. Both L1 and L3 independently pin this same junction with different tags, providing strong convergent validation. L1 (PMC8787484): HA tag inserted into full-length, membrane-anchored CD52 by replacing the peptide SQTSSP (residues 30–35), placing the tag after residue 29 (T); construct CD5HA2 expressed in human T cells and detected by FACS. L3 (PMC6395743) independently replaced the same six residues downstream of the NDT glycosylation site (residues 30–35) with a FLAG tag (CD5Flag2), confirmed by flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy (L10). Both constructs are full-length, GPI-anchored CD52 expressed on the plasma membrane.

sources.claim: We have previously demonstrated that SORTS can be adapted for the isolation of T cell populations with precisely inactivated HIV-1 genome via the KI of a CD5HA2 marker construct in which the peptide sequence SQTSSP, located in the middle of CD52, is replaced with a hemagglutinin (HA) tag ( 32 ).
sources.title: Engineering T-Cell Resistance to HIV-1 Infection via Knock-In of Peptides from the Heptad Repeat 2 Domain of gp41
